info.title: MonitorFlow public API
info.description: Scripts and integrations use `/api/v1` with an API key made under Admin › API keys: `Authorization: Bearer mfk_…`. A key acts as the administrator who made it, within its reach (everything, a customer or a site), its access and its areas. Lists that can grow take `limit` and `cursor` and answer `next_cursor`, null on the last page. Every error has `error`, plain words, and `code`, stable. Writes may carry `Idempotency-Key`; the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. A key makes up to 600 requests a minute; answers carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`, and 429 carries `Retry-After`. See ADR-0101.

404.description: Not found, or outside the key's reach: `not_found`

429.description: Over the key's rate limit: `rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`

get.description:
The 100 newest install keys of the sites whose customer the caller
administers, in every state, without their secret; and every host
waiting for approval on those sites, oldest first. Not paged; older
keys stay in the audit log.

Needs the administrator role on a customer, or global: 403 `forbidden`
otherwise, also for a site's administrator.

401.description: No key, or a key that is unknown, expired or turned off: `unauthenticated`

403.description: The caller administers no customer: `forbidden`; a key outside the "administration" area: `api_key_scope`

404.description: Not found, or outside the key's reach: `not_found`

429.description: Over the key's rate limit: `rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`

post.description:
Makes a reusable key for the install commands of a site. An `agent` key
enrolls up to `max_hosts` servers (no limit by default) until it expires
(30 days by default), each named after its host name; with
`require_approval`, each new host waits in `pending_hosts` until an
administrator approves it. A `relay` key enrolls one relay within a day
by default; `max_hosts` and `require_approval` are ignored for it, and
the relay waits for an administrator to confirm its names.

The answer is the only time the secret `token` is shown: MonitorFlow
stores its hash and no route returns it again. It comes with what the
install commands need, as for an enrollment token.

Needs the administrator role on the site's customer. A site the caller
cannot read is 404. Audited as `install_key.create`, without the secret.

Not safe to repeat: each call makes another key. With
`Idempotency-Key`, a repeat answers 409 `conflict` with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of making a second key or showing
the secret again.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID usually. The same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer instead of running twice.

Audited as `install_key.revoke`.

Needs the administrator role on the key's customer.

get.description:
The single-use tokens of the sites whose customer the caller
administers, newest first, in every state, without their secret. Records
that install keys leave when they enroll a host are not listed.

Paged: `limit` (1 to 500, default 100) and `cursor`, the `next_cursor`
of the previous page. `state` keeps only `pending`, `used` or `expired`
tokens. Unknown query parameters are refused.

Needs the administrator role on a customer, or global: 403 `forbidden`
otherwise, also for a site's administrator.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only tokens in this state.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: 1 to 500, default 100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page.

400.description: Bad `state`, `limit` or `cursor`, or an unknown parameter: `invalid`

401.description: No key, or a key that is unknown, expired or turned off: `unauthenticated`

403.description: The caller administers no customer: `forbidden`; a key outside the "administration" area: `api_key_scope`

404.description: Not found, or outside the key's reach: `not_found`

429.description: Over the key's rate limit: `rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`

post.description:
Makes a single-use token that enrolls one server (`agent`) or relay
(`relay`) under the ID `peer_id` on the site `site_id`. The answer is
the only time the secret `token` is shown: MonitorFlow stores its hash,
no route returns it again, and a token that is lost is revoked and made
again. It comes with what the install commands need: the addresses to
enroll at and connect to, and where installers download the agent from.

For a relay, `server_names` are the names and addresses its agents reach
it at; they go on its certificate. A relay token without them leaves
the relay waiting for an administrator to confirm its names (`POST
/api/v1/relays/{id}/names`).

Needs the administrator role on the site's customer. A site the caller
cannot read is 404. Audited as `enrollment_token.create`, without the
secret.

Not safe to repeat: each call makes another token. With
`Idempotency-Key`, a repeat does not make a second one but answers 409
`conflict` with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, saying the secret is shown
only once: the first answer is not stored.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID usually. The same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer instead of running twice.

400.description: A field is missing, unknown or out of range, `peer_id` is not a valid ID, `server_names` on an agent token or a name that is not a DNS name or IP address: `invalid`

401.description: No key, or a key that is unknown, expired or turned off: `unauthenticated`

403.description: The caller does not administer the site's customer: `forbidden`; a key outside the "administration" area: `api_key_scope`

404.description: No such site, or not readable by the caller: `not_found`

409.description: `peer_id` is taken by another server or relay, belongs to a peer removed from another site, or a relay name is the central server's or another site's relay's; or an `Idempotency-Key` replay: `conflict`

429.description: Over the key's rate limit: `rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`

delete.description:
Deletes a token that was not used, expired or not, so it can enroll
nothing. The audit log keeps its record (`enrollment_token.revoke`). A
used token cannot be revoked: remove the server or relay it enrolled
instead.

Needs the administrator role on the token's customer. Safe to repeat in
effect: once deleted, the token is 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The token's `id`

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID usually. The same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer instead of running twice.

401.description: No key, or a key that is unknown, expired or turned off: `unauthenticated`

403.description: The caller does not administer the token's customer: `forbidden`; a key outside the "administration" area: `api_key_scope`

404.description: No such token, already revoked, or of a site the caller cannot read: `not_found`

429.description: Over the key's rate limit: `rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`

incident_ids.description: 1 to [`MAX_LIMIT`] incidents, like a group of a notification.

Acknowledged.description:
Body of the answer: the incidents this request acknowledged. The
others were resolved, or someone acknowledged them first.

AgentInstall.description:
Body of `GET` and `PUT /api/settings/agent-install`, and the `install`
object of a new token.

oneOf.description: The release `central` commands install; `null` with nothing cached.

custom_url.description: Base URL of the `custom` source, if any.

source.description:
The default source of the install commands: `github` (the latest
public release), `central` (this server's release cache) or
`custom` (an https directory the operator gives).

source_from_config.description:
Whether the configuration sets `source` or `custom_url`, which the
web interface then cannot change.

Aggregation.description: A simple aggregation across the selected series.

AiCommandsChange.description: The last `ai_commands` command of a server, in `GET /api/servers/{id}`.

requested_by.description: The username, `null` when the account is gone.

command.description: Runs this instead of the proposal, recorded as an `edit`.

CentralRelease.description:
The newest cached release as `central` install commands pin it
(ADR-0054): its version and the SHA-256 of `SHA256SUMS`, of the
installer and of the MSI, as hex. A file is only named when the cache
holds it.

installer_sha256.description: SHA-256 of `install.sh`; `null` when the cache lacks it.

msi_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the Windows MSI; `null` when the cache lacks it.

path.description:
URL path of its files behind the web interface, without a
trailing slash: `/agent/<version>`.

CommandDetail.description:
`GET /api/commands/{id}`: the command and its output, each at most
the last 64 KiB.

health_timeout_s.description:
`self_update`: seconds the new agent has to connect before the
old one comes back; 30 to 3600, 300 by default.

packages.description: Packages to upgrade; empty or absent for all.

ttl_s.description:
Seconds the agent may still start it; [`MIN_TTL_S`] to
[`MAX_TTL_S`], default [`DEFAULT_TTL_S`].

parameters.description: The payload as JSON, for kinds the API knows.

address.description:
The address in `upstream_url` and `enroll_url`, which the tokens
page lets administrators change.

install.description: The install sources and the default one (ADR-0054).

token.description:
The secret: `mfe1.`, 43 characters of base64url, `.`, and the
pinned SHA-256 of the certificate authority in 43 more. Shown in
this answer only; MonitorFlow keeps only its hash.

CreatedEnrollmentToken.description:
Body of `POST /api/tokens`: the stored token, its secret string and the
peer configuration it needs. Shown once; nothing returns it again. No
`Debug`, so the secret cannot end up in a log line.

install.description: The install sources and the default one.

token.description:
The secret, in the same `mfe1.…` form as an enrollment token. Shown
in this answer only; MonitorFlow keeps only its hash.

CreatedInstallKey.description:
Body of `POST /api/install-keys`: the stored key, its secret string,
named `token` as installers take it, and what the commands need. Shown
once; no `Debug`, so the secret cannot end up in a log line.

site_count.description: Sites of the customer the user reads, not all of them.

command.description: What will run, or what was rejected.

EnrollmentToken.description: One token, never with its secret.

created_by.description: `null` for tokens made with the server CLI.

created_by_username.description:
`null` for tokens made with the server CLI, or when that user was
deleted.

peer_id.description: The ID the enrolled server or relay gets.

server_names.description:
Relay tokens: the names its certificate will carry. Empty for
agents.

used_at.description: When a host enrolled with it; `null` while unused.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

peer_id.description:
The ID the server or relay will have: its certificate name, 1 to 64
ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. An ID another server or
relay holds is refused.

server_names.description:
Relays only, at most 16: the DNS names and IP addresses its agents
connect to, which its certificate will carry. The central server's
own names and names another site's relay holds are refused. Empty
for agents.

ttl_s.description:
Validity in seconds, 60 to 604800 (7 days); 3600 (one hour) when
absent or `null`.

EnrollmentTokenState.description: `pending` until used or expired; a used token stays `used`.

details.description:
For instance `{"reason": "threshold_removed"}`, `{"notified":
true}` when a silence ended, `{"username", "via"}` when
acknowledged, or `{"step", "steps", "minutes", "told"}` for a
follow-up step.

kind.description:
`opened`, `escalated`, `deescalated`, `resolved`, what a silence
did: `silenced` and `silence_ended` (ADR-0079), `acknowledged`, and
`followed_up` when a follow-up step told someone (ADR-0082).

occurred_at.description: Sample time of the change, or the server clock without a sample.

severity.description: Severity after the change; `null` once resolved.

FollowUpView.description: Where an incident is in its follow-up.

next.description: Who it would tell then, people first; empty when nobody can be.

next_at.description: When the next step is told if nobody acknowledges.

started_at.description: When the first message went out.

state.description:
`waiting` for the next step at `next_at`, `silenced` until a silence
ends then waiting, or `stopped`.

step.description: Steps told so far, and how many there are now.

stop_reason.description:
When stopped: `acknowledged`, `resolved`, `not_critical`, or
`finished` once every step was told.

GroupView.description: A notification that told this incident with others (ADR-0080).

incidents.description:
How many incidents it told that the user may read, this one
included. Members on sites outside the user's scope are not counted.

GuestKind.description: What a Proxmox guest is, which picks its API path.

oneOf.description:
Who is told next if nobody acknowledges (ADR-0082); `null` when no
follow-up started: a warning, or not sent yet.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

IncidentView.description:
One incident. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

acknowledged_by.description:
Who said they are on it, and when (ADR-0082); `null` until someone
does. The name stays when the account is removed.

can_acknowledge.description:
Whether the reader may acknowledge it: open, not acknowledged, and
the reader an operator or above of its site.

hostname.description: The server's hostname, or the relay's name.

instance.description: `""` for a series without an instance.

metric.description: `offline` when the server or relay stopped reporting (ADR-0072).

opened_at.description: Sample times, not the server clock.

peak_value.description: The worst value seen while open.

relay_id.description: Set for a relay's offline incident only (ADR-0072).

severity.description: `warning` or `critical`; the last one while resolved.

silenced.description: Whether a silence ever held back a notification of it.

silenced_until.description:
While open and covered by a silence, when the last one ends
(ADR-0079).

threshold.description: The threshold as it was when the incident opened.

InstallKey.description: One key, never with its secret.

created_by_username.description:
`null` for keys made with the server CLI, or when that user was
deleted.

max_hosts.description: Hosts it may enroll; `null` for no limit. 1 for a relay key.

keys.description:
The 100 newest keys, revoked and expired ones included, newest
first.

pending_hosts.description: Every host waiting for approval, oldest first.

max_hosts.description:
Hosts the key may enroll, 1 to 100000; no limit when absent or
`null`. Ignored for a relay key, which enrolls one host.

require_approval.description:
New hosts wait for an administrator before they appear (see
`pending_hosts`). `false` by default; ignored for a relay key.

role.description:
`agent` by default. A `relay` key enrolls one relay, whose names an
administrator confirms (ADR-0066), so it takes no host limit or
approval.

ttl_s.description:
Validity in seconds, 3600 (one hour) to 31536000 (one year);
2592000 (30 days) by default, 86400 (one day) for a relay.

InstallKeyState.description:
`revoked` first, then `expired`, then `used_up` once `host_count`
reaches `max_hosts`; `active` otherwise. Only `active` keys enroll.

PendingHost.description: A host enrolled by a key that asks for approval.

peer_id.description: The ID it was given, which approving or rejecting it takes.

source.description: The IP address it enrolled from; `null` when unknown.

PendingView.description:
One command waiting for approval. Field names and types are part of
the API contract: add fields, never rename or remove them.

can_approve.description:
Whether the user may approve this command as proposed, and reject
it. UX hints: the decision routes check again.

command.description: The proposed command, exactly as it would run.

commands_run.description: Commands the incident ran so far, and its limit.

deadline.description:
`opened_at + max_duration_s`: the incident escalates then, and a
decision after it is 409.

diagnosis.description: The AI's text: untrusted, shown as data.

id.description: The pending command; decisions go to `/approvals/{id}/...`.

shell.description:
What runs the command: `posix` (`/bin/sh`) or `powershell`
(Windows PowerShell), from the server's system (ADR-0084).

shell_acceptance.description:
What the server's agent last said it does with these commands:
`accepted`, `off`, `unsupported`, or `null` when unknown (ADR-0076).
Approving is 409 once it refuses them.

snapshots.description:
Whether a change on this server is snapshotted first, on Proxmox
(ADR-0044) or locally (ADR-0094); when not, rollback is limited.

tier.description: `low_impact` or `high_impact`, from the rules, never from the AI.

PublicAddress.description:
Body of `GET` and `PUT /api/settings/public-address`, and the
`address` object of a new token.

address.description: The address in the install commands.

certified.description:
Whether the certificate is issued for `address`; agents refuse to
connect otherwise.

default.description: The first server name, used when none is chosen.

names.description: The names the server's certificate is issued for.

upstream_url.description:
`upstream_url` and `enroll_url` at `address`, with the published
ports.

query.description: The PromQL the API ran, filters included.

reason.description: Sent back to the AI with the rejection, and recorded.

Rollup.description:
How each point of a range summarizes the samples since the previous
point. Without it, a point is the last sample before it, so a spike
between two points of a long range is not drawn.

SeriesView.description:
One series: its labels and its `[unix seconds, value]` points. A value
that is not finite is `null`.

oneOf.description:
The last time AI commands were turned on or off from the web
interface, `null` if never (ADR-0098).

The certificate issued last to this agent, revoked or not; `null`
when the CA never issued one (a server row created by hand).

ServerDetail.description:
Body of `GET /api/servers/{id}`: the listing row plus the agent's
current certificate.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

ServerView.description:
One server. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

agent_version.description: Version reported by the live stream, else the one last stored.

cert_not_after.description:
Latest expiry among the agent's unrevoked certificates; `null` when
it has none. Past dates mean every certificate has expired.

command_kinds.description:
What its agent last said it does with each command kind: `accepted`,
`off` or `unsupported` (ADR-0076). `null`, or a kind missing here, is
unknown: its agent or a relay on the way does not report yet.

connected_at.description: Start of the current stream, when online.

last_heartbeat.description:
Last message received: from the live stream when online, else the
last time recorded in the database.

offline_alerts.description:
Whether it opens an incident when offline (ADR-0072); muted when
this or `site_offline_alerts` is `false`.

open_incidents.description: Threshold and offline incidents currently open on this server.

package_updates.description: Whether the host can take package updates and sources (ADR-0063).

silenced_until.description: While a silence covers it, when the last one ends (ADR-0079).

via_relay.description: Peer ID of the relay carrying the live stream, if any.

Shell.description: The shell that runs a server's commands, which decides the rules.

target_id.description: The server, relay, site or customer; absent for `all`.

can_end.description: Whether this user may end it.

agent_auto_update.description:
The site's automatic update override: `null` follows the
server-wide setting (ADR-0055).

agent_auto_update_effective.description: Whether automatic updates apply to the site, override or not.

offline_alerts.description:
Whether servers and relays of the site open incidents when offline
(ADR-0072).

relay_count.description: Enrolled relays of the site, revoked ones included (ADR-0029).

SnapshotSupport.description:
Whether the server can be snapshotted; without it the interface shows
that rollback is limited.

detail.description:
With `cannot_snapshot`: what Proxmox cannot snapshot, like "rootfs
is on storage local (dir), which cannot take snapshots".

oneOf.description: The mapped guest's kind, so the reason can say VM or container.

left_out.description: What a snapshot does not hold, though Proxmox takes one.

method.description:
Which snapshot a change gets when available: `proxmox`, or a local
`lvm` or `zfs` snapshot (ADR-0094).

Tier.description: Risk tiers of architecture §8, from least to most dangerous.

TokenRole.description: What the token enrolls: `agent` for a server, `relay` for a relay.

tags.name: remediation
tags.description: Commands the AI proposed, waiting for a person

tags.name: metrics
tags.description: Metric queries built by MonitorFlow, never raw PromQL

tags.name: enrollment
tags.description: Bringing servers and relays into MonitorFlow. An enrollment token is single-use: it enrolls one named server or relay on one site within its validity (one hour by default). An install key is reusable: it enrolls any number of servers (or one relay) on one site for up to a year, names each after its host, and can make new hosts wait for an administrator's approval. Both are secrets shown once, in the answer that creates them; no route returns them again and an `Idempotency-Key` replay does not either. Every route needs the administrator role on the site's customer, given globally or for that customer: a site's administrator cannot enroll. Through an API key, that means access "Administer", the "administration" area, and a reach of everything or of the customer.
